- If sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon.
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion speed — adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% lagged error to next forecast.
- If true outcome is below model by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction of 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict late-period values — reduce final 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative momentum, model often fails to capture downward drift — add 1–3% downward adjustment to all forecasts.
